title: First march of the Madres de Plaza de Mayo
summary: On Saturday 30 April 1977, mothers of people who had disappeared under Argentina's military dictatorship (1976 to 1983) met in Plaza de Mayo in front of the Casa Rosada. Told they could not stand still, they began walking in circles. The marches became a weekly Thursday ritual that carried on for decades.

uncertainty.note: The first meeting is dated 30 April 1977; the marches continued weekly, paused only during the pandemic (Buenos Aires Herald).

importance.justification: The start of a long-running public protest by relatives of the disappeared under Argentina's military dictatorship.

audience_note: Concerns enforced disappearances under a military dictatorship, including the disappearance of three of the group's founders.
